findings.reason: a node implementing the section as written would key the grant on a finding shape that the motivating incident never had, and the same block would recur on the next repair round that names a source file and asks for a test.
findings.text: §27's *Why* states "The finding named no `file`", but the blocking finding in the cited review record carries `file: reckon/crew/merge.py, line: 108`, and the round's own advice names it that way ("[f47f2e19580] reckon/crew/merge.py:108 The new merge refusal has no committed regression test …", resume-1-advice.txt), with the round's write scope `reckon/crew/merge.py, reckon/crew/promotion.py, reckon/crew_run_commands.py, docs/evidence/…, docs/figures/…` and no `tests/` path; the deliverable's condition ("names no `file`") therefore does not fire on the incident it cites, because the failure is a finding whose `file` names the *source* the test must cover while the change the finding asks for is a *different* path (`tests/test_merge_requires_promotable_run.py`)

findings.reason: done-when case 1 cannot pass without also relaxing the decline-only predicate, which the section neither names nor grants as in-scope work, so the node would either fail its own gate or change a gate the plan did not authorise.
findings.text: even under §27's own premise, a fileless blocking finding never reaches `_grant_round_scope`: `compose_repair_for_run` returns decline-only before it when no blocking finding cites a repairable path (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1130-1148`, `if not _repairable_scope((str(finding.get("file") or "") for finding in blocking), fence=run_fence): … status="decline-only" … return`), and `_grant_round_scope` is only called at :1312 past that return, so a review carrying only the fileless finding the done-when describes dispatches no round and grants nothing

findings.reason: the two cases together are the whole measure, and with `<node>` and the predicate unstated the implementer chooses both, so the test proves the implementation it wrote rather than the one the plan asked for.
findings.text: "one new test file named after the node, `tests/test_<node>.py`" leaves `<node>` undefined (the repair node id from `repair_node_id`, reckon/crew/repair.py:434-450, is a round id carrying the reviewed head sha, not the reviewed run's node), and "its text says a test is missing or uncommitted" names no reader or predicate, so the done-when's first case cannot assert a literal path and its second case — "a blocking finding with no `file` about anything else grants no test path" — is separated from the first by an unstated rule
